This encoder rejects TargetCollection, but Table.InsertMany currently serializes rows using TargetCollection (astra/table.go:165). As a result, inserting datatypes.Duration via Table.InsertMany will fail (including this PR’s integration test) even though it’s a table-only type. Consider switching Table.InsertMany to use TargetTable, or otherwise ensuring table insertMany uses the table target.

body: ISO 8601 fractional seconds parsing can overflow for long fractions because it parses the entire digit string into int64 and ignores errors. For very long fractions (valid ISO 8601), strconv.ParseInt will overflow and this code will incorrectly compute nanoseconds (often 0). Truncate/pad to 9 digits before parsing so sub-nanosecond precision is safely truncated without overflow.

DurationBuilder.addNanos allows negative values. That can produce mixed-sign durations (violating the type invariant) and can also break the overflow check via int64 overflow when b.nanoseconds becomes negative (MaxNanos - b.nanoseconds). Reject negative inputs and require callers to use Negate()/SetNegative() instead.
